title: Retyped pages: bass battles and Jimmy Blanton
summary: Repeat of the talk on bass contests and Blanton's technique.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. You were talking about some of the contests. Do you remember any in particular on bass that stay in your mind?
Battles?
Yeah, that you were involved in or that you listened to.
Well, the best I ever played was Oscar came to San Francisco with Duke and Vern Ellis (inaudible) jam session.
Uh-huh.
(Inaudible), but I played exceptionally well.
Who were the other players?
Nobody but me.
Oh, I see, yes. Do you remember any times when there were contests, that you were exceptionally good?
No, I wasn't in -- the best ever was Jimmy Blanton, Sam Stuart, Red Calendar (inaudible), just no competition.
You mean in terms of Blanton?
What we was doing.
Yeah. That's what I wanted to ask you about. I only heard him on records, I never heard him live. Why was Blanton so important? What was he doing that nobody had done before?
(Inaudible.)
Anything else beside that?
Well, a lot of guys -- see, like, Eddie Gomez, they can (inaudible), but they don't. They only play up high. Some musicians (inaudible), but Jimmy Blanton played up high and down low, (inaudible).
And the guys before him, aside from covering the whole instrument, I guess -- was their rhythm different than Blanton? Did he loosen up the rhythm?
(Inaudible) by Walter Page.
Did you get to talk to --
Very little technique. Just sliding down the strings.
Jazz bass players made the bass (inaudible).
Yeah.
There are some classical bass players who are out there by themselves -- I forgot their names. Like __________, who was a beginner playing bass (inaudible).
I know. When I was a kid, I got some recordings of his, solo bass, and compared it to Blanton, to you, to Scott Lethero, it was like kindergarten.
It was written in G, played in the key of G and the key of D minor. That was about it. Playing the keys that are simple for bass.
Yeah.
Blanton played in all keys, in D flat, G flat, B natural.
